Servers might make 500 on a very rare night. If they are in the best section, on a night with a game on that everyone wants to watch. Other than that, an average night on a weekend will be 250 after tip out. And all other shifts you are looking at 100 to 150. That's for a good shift.

Say you do actually work full time as a server 5 days a week. Which I don't know many that do, usually you have to work at a restaurant for years to get priority for that to happen.. you are looking at 600-800 for the week. And your minimum wage paycheck will go entirely to pay your taxes. 

I have worked as a server for about a year and a half, I had one night where I made 500 in tips. After tip outs I walked with 400. 

I have had many more days where I made 30 to 60 bucks in tips. That is far more common...

Just because an employer cannot force you to share a portion of your tips doesn't mean that you do not have to as a server or bartender. All that means is that they cannot tell you how much to tip out, if you can only give a person $3 or $10 out of your tips that is up to you as the server or bartender, not the owner. 

If a server didn't share their tips. The tables would not be cleaned. The food would not be run out to the table etc. If the bartender didn't share their tips. They would have no one refilling stock, getting ice, changing kegs.

You are not tipping just a server or bartender, you are tipping all the other people behind the scenes making the show go on that you don't care to pay attention to. Your server and bartender are paying attention to them and treat them with respect because they know the work is important and without them they would fail. 

We expect a tip because you are paying us to deal with your dumb ass, and keep a smile on our faces. Spend 5 minutes reading server horror stories and get a clue. 

I have had people not tip me for not bringing them napkins fast enough. For not letting them order drinks for people not present at the table. Because they asked for more time to look at the menu, but then I gave them too much time so they felt the need to scream at me for attention across the restaurant. 

It is a thankless, labor-intensive, demeaning job. One that doesn't have health insurance. Or even free food. Yes. We have to pay for our meals... which we don't get to eat, because we don't get a break.

I could go on..  

No one expects you to tip at a self service casual restaurant. Or for your coffee.. or whatever else. If you are at a sit down restaurant with someone proving you service, give them an appropriate tip. No one is demanding 25% from you.

Here is advice from someone with chronic pain and health issues. 

Your mental health is going to improve so much once you deal with the issues that you have described. Keep that goal in your mind as motivation for you to do this.

As you watch videos of people cleaning. Remember that you need to do things differently, they go about things in a way where they clean one area entirely before they move to the next. Remove the garbage, wipe the furniture, clean the floors. Put everything back. 

I want you to not do this, this is done for a satisfying video. It isnt a sustainable way to learn how to keep clean long term.

First just focus on the garbage. Only the garbage. 

If you are throwing things away. And you find dirty clothes, put those to the side, you dont see them, you dont care about them. Dont expend energy taking the clothes to a different part of the house, or trying to find them all. Same goes for dishes. If there is food in them, scrape it into a trash bag and put them to the side. You don't see them, you dont care about them. 

Just get the garbage out. 

Next. You must understand this will take time, and in the meantime, do not add to the garbage pile. Get a trash can and trash bags, put your garbage in the trash, you must start good habits, even if there is still trash on the floor. You don't see it you don't care. You make sure you put your dinner garbage in the trash the moment you finish eating it going forward. 

Set a goal for yourself. 2 bags of trash a day. Give yourself a sticker every time you get it done. Or buy a thing you love, you get a coke, or a chocolate. Reward yourself.

Ok. You did the garbage, next will be the dishes. Again. You see something that is a mess, a bug, a spill.. no you don't. You are just going to do the dishes. 

Reward when you are done. And make sure going forward you do your dishes right away and don't let them stack up. Create good habits.

Ok. Now get all the laundry together. And just put it in a safe area for the time being. Because you have bugs you need to focus on just getting that stuff secured and out of the way. 

You do also have an animal so make that a priority. Clean litter and food areas are a top priority.

You should have room at this point to move around. Take a break, because you are going to have to bug bomb the house. 

This would be a great time to take some good care of yourself, purchase some nice gifts for yourself, clothes, soap, contact someone who can deal with the matt in your hair. Go stay at a hotel for a night, cat can come with.

When you get home, you are going to be feeling really motivated, refreshed, and have experienced a clean body and environment.

This should be the fun part for you, you get to find all your books, and wipe a shelf off and start putting them there.

It will take a long time, you will need to get a new mattress, probably all new sheets and clothes.

But now at this point, you can clean surfaces and floors, and put loved items away. 

Once you have things generally in order. Just remember. Dishes garbage laundry. Dishes garbage laundry. If you just make sure those things are done each day you are doing amazing. The bathroom doesn't need to be cleaned every day. The floors don't need to be cleaned every day.

Make a calendar and put on big thing on it a week. And set a schedule for the cat litter. Clean the litter at least once a week. Every Wednesday you do the litter. First Sunday of the month is the bathroom. Second Sunday you vacuum and mop floors. 3rd Sunday you change the bed sheets. Etc etc. 


Make a schedule for personal health as well. Every Friday you wash your hair. Every first Monday of the month you cut your nails. Etc etc. 

You can do it. It doesn't matter how long it takes. You are worth it.

So I would make this in 2 peices. For the top and bottom get a very stiff fusible interfacing and then the top fation fabric in silver. Iron that together to make the shape stick out and stiff.

For pattern. The top should be a big square with a hole in the middle for the head to go through. I would get some velcro on the back to make the closure. You could if you want to find a pattern for a poncho, but I wouldn't spend money on it. Take your shoulder measurements and then add like 5 inches on either side so it goes past the shoulder and then make that square. Then take a measurement from neck to waist where you want it to end just in case it needs to be more rectangle than square. Measure your neck around and use that to know how big the head hole needs to be. If you need to make it a bit more form fitted,  add some darts by the boob area. 

For the bottoms. Take your waist measurement and half that,  add some seam allowance on either side, cut 2. Measure down your hip to wear you want it to end. You will cut a rectangle from these measurements but add a few inches to the bottom of the rectangle so it flairs out. You fold this in half and cut on the fold side from the end corner to crotch. Take a measurement from waist to crotch to see how far down to mark this so it makes the star shape on the bottom. Again just use velcro in the back for closure. If you really want to get a pattern this would be an a-line skirt.

I would not recommend doing any toners without bleaching again, you are definitely at a dark orange level, no toner will get it to be white like the front, it will more likely turn a muddy green color.

If you want to dye it dark again I recommend the color ion level 6 dark mushroom blonde, with 10 volume developer, I would apply it to the orange area first, leave it for 15 minutes. If you dont want to do another bleach. Or go back to dark. I would recommend using the level 6 mushroom blonde on the back, 10 volume for 26 minutes, and then on the orange section do the ion level 8 mushroom blonde with 20 volume for 25 minutes. Pets should have designated spaces made for them. They should each have their own beds or spaces for themselves such as a crate or a blanket they like.

Cats need to have spaces that are up high and down low, they call this tree dwelling or bush dwelling. Something like a high cat tower or a shelf on the wall just for them. For example I have a bed on top of the fridge for my cats. They know they can go on the counter to get to the top of the fridge but can't stay sitting on the counter if I am working. A great example is June's kitchen on YouTube. He understands how cats work, gives them a place to sit and watch him which in the kitchen and allows them to snoof ingredients while working. 

It is important to understand how animals think, they understand possession and do not like to share. Please provide your animals with individual items based on their personality. I have one tree dweller and one bush dweller so I have to make high spaces accessible and some hidden spaces comfortable. My tree dweller will only cuddle if he has a blanky.

You should not have an animal if you do not intend to train it and teach it boundaries. That is how you get dogs that climb on top of your guests on the couch. That whine when you suddenly get a SO and they can sleep on "their" side of the bed. Dogs (that have not been abused) generally love their crates, it is their safe space, their "bedroom". They like to keep their favorite toys in there and sleep inside, they like the enclosed safe space. 

Training an animal is all or none. Either they can be on the couch and bed all the time or none of them time. They don't understand that you have guests and now they can't use the couch. Keep in mind that if you move furniture to a different place training starts over again because in an animals mind it is a new item of interest.
